title: Brown Rice with Dark Green Vegetables and Tomatoes

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain product that retains the bran and germ. Combined with dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach) and tomatoes or a tomato‑based sauce, it creates a nutritious dish with no added fat. The combination is rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice keeps more nutrients than white rice because the bran layer remains intact.
Dark green vegetables contain chlorophyll, which supports the body’s detoxification processes.
Tomatoes are a major source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Fat‑free dishes often rely on the natural moisture of vegetables and tomato juice for flavor.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nervous system health, and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Brown rice provides thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene and vitamin C from tomatoes
items.content: They help strengthen the immune system and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in added fat
items.content: The absence of added fats makes the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Tomato allergy caution
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato products.

items.title: Possible trace heavy metals
items.content: Like many whole grains, rice can accumulate small amounts of cadmium or arsenic; choose reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook brown rice until tender, steam dark green vegetables, and add fresh tomatoes or a low‑fat tomato sauce. The dish can be served as a side or a main course, paired with lean proteins such as chicken, fish, or legumes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked dishes should be kept in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days and reheated thoroughly before serving.
